entries.affected: Contracting authorities and suppliers in defence and security procurement under Directive 2009/81/EC; transfers of defence products between Member States.

source.quote: 09/10/2026 Act adopted by Council after Parliament's 1st reading
source.ref: European Parliament, Legislative Observatory, procedure 2025/0177(COD), key events

entries.title: Defence procurement directive: the simplification amendment is adopted by Parliament and Council
entries.whatChanged: The directive amending Directives 2009/43/EC (transfers of defence products within the Union) and 2009/81/EC (defence and security procurement) passed the European Parliament at first reading on 16 September 2026 and was adopted by the Council on 9 October 2026. The Legislative Observatory lists it as awaiting signature. It is not yet published in the Official Journal and not in force. We have not compared the final text with the Commission's proposal.

entries.affected: Ukrainian companies deciding whether to join a consortium for an EDF call, and EU coordinators who would take them in.

source.quote: Participation of entities established in Ukraine is pending the signature of the association agreement to EDF (see countries currently negotiating association agreements below).
source.ref: European Commission, EDF call document EDF-2026-DA (version 1.3 of 8 September 2026), section 6, footnote to "Eligible participants"; the same footnote is in the other nine EDF call documents of 2026. Also: European Commission, DG DEFIS, Support to Ukraine (page without a date; read on 18 October 2026)

entries.title: EDF: Ukraine's association is pending the signature of the agreement (not confirmed in force)
entries.whatChanged: The EDF call documents of 2026 say, in a footnote to the list of countries associated to the EDF, that participation of entities established in Ukraine is pending the signature of the association agreement to the EDF (10 of 10 call documents read, the latest versions dated 8 September 2026). The Commission's page on support to Ukraine, which carries no date, says Ukraine "has been fully associated" to the European Defence Fund. We found no Official Journal text of the agreement, no Council decision on it and no notice of its entry into force, and steps taken in Ukraine, as the press reports them, do not settle the EU side. Until a primary text settles it, the readiness check treats a company established in Ukraine as conditional on the association agreement for the EDF, and DefenceGate marks no European Defence Fund call as open to Ukraine or as closed to it. The calls of EDIP's Ukraine Support Instrument, which the portal files under the EDF (topic codes EDF-EDIP-USI-), are another instrument: they are labelled EDIP USI on the funding pages and marked open to Ukraine.

entries.affected: Canadian suppliers, who may take part in SAFE procurement on the agreement's terms, and EU suppliers competing with them.

source.quote: The Agreement between the European Union and Canada laying down the conditions for the participation of Canadian legal entities and products originating in Canada to procurement under the SAFE Instrument is hereby approved.
source.ref: Council Decision (EU) 2026/1381 of 15 June 2026, Article 1 and recital (1); Official Journal L, 18.6.2026. The agreement: OJ L 2026/445, Article 5

entries.title: SAFE: the agreement with Canada is concluded
entries.whatChanged: The Council approved the agreement between the European Union and Canada on the participation of Canadian legal entities and Canadian products in SAFE procurement on 15 June 2026 (Decision (EU) 2026/1381, published 18 June 2026). According to that decision, the agreement was signed on 14 February 2026 and has been applied provisionally from 13 April 2026; the agreement itself is published as OJ L 2026/445 (3 March 2026). Its Article 5 sets the conditions: a Canadian legal entity must be established in Canada and have its executive management structures in Canada, the Union, an EEA EFTA State or Ukraine, and must not be controlled by a third country (a guarantee verified by a Member State is the derogation); components originating in Canada may exceed 35 % of the component cost, at least 20 % must originate in the Union, an EEA EFTA State or Ukraine, and the cost of components from third countries may not exceed the cost of those from the Union, an EEA EFTA State or Ukraine, and in any case 35 %. The decision says the date of entry into force will be published in the Official Journal by the Council's General Secretariat; we have not found that notice. The readiness check treats a Canadian company as conditional for SAFE on these terms.

entries.affected: Suppliers in EDIP common procurement, industrial reinforcement and supporting actions, and Ukrainian and EU suppliers in the Ukraine Support Instrument.

source.quote: The financial envelopes for the implementation of the Programme for the period from 30 December 2025 to 31 December 2027 shall be composed of: (a) EUR 1 200 000 000 in current prices; and (b) additional contributions in accordance with Article 5.

entries.title: EDIP Regulation in force: EUR 1.2 billion for the Programme and EUR 300 million for Ukraine
entries.whatChanged: Regulation (EU) 2025/2643 establishing the European Defence Industry Programme was adopted on 16 December 2025 and published on 29 December 2025, so it entered into force on 30 December 2025. For 30 December 2025 to 31 December 2027 the Programme has EUR 1 200 000 000 in current prices and the Ukraine Support Instrument EUR 300 000 000 in current prices (Article 3), plus additional contributions.

entries.affected: Ukrainian and EU companies applying to calls of the Ukraine Support Instrument (their topic codes start with EDF-EDIP-USI).

links.label: Calls of the Ukraine Support Instrument (EDIP USI)

source.quote: Only legal entities established in the Union or in Ukraine and having their executive management structures in the Union or in Ukraine shall be eligible to be recipients of Union funding under this Regulation.

entries.title: Ukraine Support Instrument: open to entities established in Ukraine
entries.whatChanged: Under the Ukraine Support Instrument of EDIP only legal entities established in the Union or in Ukraine, with their executive management structures in the Union or in Ukraine, are eligible for funding. Entities established in the non-government-controlled areas of Ukraine are not. DefenceGate marks the funding calls of this instrument as open to Ukraine.

entries.affected: Manufacturers and component suppliers in EDIP common procurement and industrial reinforcement actions.

source.quote: For procurement carried out pursuant to Articles 11, 13 and 35 which is supported by Union funding, the cost of components originating outside the Union and associated countries shall not be higher than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product.

entries.title: EDIP: at most 35 % of component cost from outside the Union and associated countries
entries.whatChanged: For EDIP procurement supported by Union funding the cost of components originating outside the Union and associated countries may not exceed 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product, and no component may come from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States. Article 10(4) sets the same share for industrial reinforcement actions. The readiness check applies it (rule “Components from outside the Union and associated countries: at most 35 % of component cost”).

entries.affected: Manufacturers and component suppliers in calls of the Ukraine Support Instrument.

source.quote: For procurement carried out pursuant to paragraph 1, points (a) and (c), which is supported by Union funding, the cost of components originating outside the Union and Ukraine shall not be higher than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product.

entries.title: Ukraine Support Instrument: at most 35 % of component cost from outside the Union and Ukraine
entries.whatChanged: For procurement supported under the Ukraine Support Instrument the cost of components originating outside the Union and Ukraine may not exceed 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product, and no component may come from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States. Article 27(4) sets the same share for industrial reinforcement actions. The readiness check applies it (rule “Components from outside the Union and Ukraine: at most 35 % of component cost”).

entries.affected: Companies that look at the EDIP common procurement calls (the calls whose topic code contains CPA) as applicants, and the contracting authorities that would lead them.

source.quote: Only the following legal entities shall be eligible for common procurement actions:

entries.title: EDIP common procurement: only contracting authorities, international organisations, SEAPs and the EDA may apply
entries.whatChanged: Under Article 11(2) of Regulation (EU) 2025/2643 only contracting authorities of Member States or associated countries, international organisations, SEAPs (structures for European armament programmes) and the European Defence Agency are eligible for common procurement actions. A company or a research body cannot apply to a call of that kind (the EDIP calls whose topic code contains CPA); it can take part in other roles, such as associated partner or subcontractor, as the call documents say. Industrial reinforcement actions (Article 12) are not under this rule.

entries.affected: Ukrainian companies and EU companies that would form consortia with them in EDF calls.

source.quote: Ukraine, in accordance with the conditions laid down in the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement.
source.ref: Regulation (EU) 2025/2653, Article 3(1), replacing Article 5 of Regulation (EU) 2021/697

entries.title: EDF: Ukraine can be an associated country
entries.whatChanged: Regulation (EU) 2025/2653, published on 22 December 2025 and in force from 23 December 2025, replaced Article 5 of the European Defence Fund Regulation. The Fund is now open to the participation of EEA EFTA members, and of Ukraine in accordance with the conditions laid down in the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement. The text makes Ukraine's participation possible; it does not say that the conditions are met (next entry).

entries.affected: United Kingdom suppliers, and EU suppliers that work with them in SAFE procurements.

source.quote: However, we have not been able to conclude these negotiations with an agreement.
source.ref: UK Parliament, written statement HCWS1114, Statement on UK-EU Relations, Paymaster General and Minister for the Cabinet Office, 1 December 2025 (text read through the Parliament's public written-statements API on 18 October 2026; the web page itself is behind a bot check)

entries.title: SAFE: no agreement with the United Kingdom (UK government statement of 1 December 2025)
entries.whatChanged: On 18 September 2025 the Council authorised the Commission to open negotiations with the United Kingdom and with Canada on their participation in SAFE (Decision (EU) 2025/2134). For Canada they ended in the agreement above. For the United Kingdom, a written statement of the UK government to Parliament on 1 December 2025 (HCWS1114) says the UK and the EU had not been able to conclude the negotiations with an agreement, and that UK companies continue to have access to SAFE under standard third-country terms, which the statement puts at up to 35 % of their content. That matches Article 16 of the SAFE Regulation, which treats United Kingdom entities like those of any other third country. We found no later primary text (an agreement, a signature or a new round), so what holds after 1 December 2025 is unconfirmed.

entries.affected: Contracting authorities and suppliers in defence and security procurement.

source.quote: the Defence Readiness Roadmap of October 2025 announced the upcoming revision of the legal framework.
source.ref: European Commission, DG DEFIS, Simplifying EU rules on defence and sensitive security procurement, 25 November 2025

entries.title: Defence procurement directive: a fuller revision is announced
entries.whatChanged: The Commission says the Defence Readiness Roadmap of October 2025 announced the upcoming revision of the legal framework of Directive 2009/81/EC, a separate initiative from the simplification amendment above. We found no published proposal at the date checked, so we state neither its content nor whether it will include a preference for European products.

entries.affected: Contracting authorities and suppliers in defence and security procurement.

source.quote: The rules governing framework procurement agreements will be clarified, and the maximum duration of a framework agreement will be extended from 7 to 10 years.
source.ref: Commission proposal COM(2025) 823 final of 17 June 2025, explanatory memorandum; thresholds in the operative text

entries.title: Defence procurement directive: the Commission's proposal of 17 June 2025
entries.whatChanged: The Commission proposed to raise the thresholds of Directive 2009/81/EC (point (a) of Article 8 from EUR 443 000 to EUR 900 000, point (b) from EUR 5 538 000 to EUR 7 000 000) and to extend the maximum duration of a framework agreement from 7 to 10 years. These are the figures of the proposal; the adopted text may differ and we have not checked it.

entries.affected: Member States that request SAFE loans, and the contractors and subcontractors in the common procurements those loans pay for.

source.quote: This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
source.ref: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106, the final Article; Official Journal L, 28.5.2025

entries.title: SAFE Regulation in force: EUR 150 billion of loans for common defence procurement
entries.whatChanged: Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1106 was adopted on 27 May 2025 and published in the Official Journal on 28 May 2025, so it entered into force on 29 May 2025. The maximum amount of financial assistance in the form of loans under SAFE is EUR 150 000 000 000.

entries.affected: Contractors, and the subcontractors involved in a SAFE common procurement: legal entities that provide critical inputs, are allocated at least 15 % of the value of the contract and need access to classified information (Article 16(12)). Other suppliers are not bound by this paragraph, but the components they supply count towards the 35 % limit on the end product.

source.quote: Contractors and subcontractors involved in the common procurement shall be established and have their executive management structures in the Union, in an EEA EFTA State or in Ukraine.

entries.title: SAFE: who may be a contractor or subcontractor
entries.whatChanged: Contractors and subcontractors involved in a SAFE common procurement must be established, and have their executive management, in the Union, an EEA EFTA State or Ukraine, and must not be controlled from another third country. Article 16(5) allows a derogation for an entity established in the Union that is controlled from elsewhere, if it was screened under the investment-screening Regulation or provides guarantees verified by the Member State.

entries.affected: Manufacturers of end products sold in SAFE-financed procurements, and their component suppliers.

source.quote: The cost of components originating outside the Union, EEA EFTA States and Ukraine shall not be higher than 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product. For the purpose of procurements supported by the SAFE instrument, no component shall be sourced from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States.

entries.title: SAFE: at most 35 % of component cost from outside the Union, EEA EFTA States and Ukraine
entries.whatChanged: In a SAFE-supported procurement the cost of components originating outside the Union, the EEA EFTA States and Ukraine may not exceed 35 % of the estimated cost of the components of the end product, and no component may be sourced from a third country that contravenes the security and defence interests of the Union and its Member States. These are two rules: a threshold and a categorical exclusion.

entries.affected: Suppliers from countries with a Security and Defence Partnership, and EU suppliers who would meet their competition in SAFE procurements.

source.quote: The Union may conclude bilateral or multilateral agreements with acceding, potential candidate and candidate countries other than Ukraine and other third countries with which the Union has entered into a Security and Defence Partnership (NBI) in order to open the eligibility conditions referred to in Article 16 to those countries and their territories, in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article.

entries.title: SAFE can be opened to other third countries by agreement (Article 17)
entries.whatChanged: The Union may conclude agreements with acceding, candidate and potential candidate countries other than Ukraine, and with other third countries that have a Security and Defence Partnership with the Union, to open SAFE's eligibility conditions to them. Each agreement says how the conditions of Article 16 apply (location of management, control, location of infrastructure, share of components).

entries.affected: Exporters of dual-use items from the Union.

source.quote: An authorisation shall be required for the export of dual-use items listed in Annex I.

entries.title: Dual-use export control: authorisation for items in Annex I (in force since 2021)
entries.whatChanged: Regulation (EU) 2021/821 requires an authorisation for the export of dual-use items listed in its Annex I. It was published on 11 June 2021 and entered into force on the ninetieth day after publication, 9 September 2021. We list it because the requirements catalogue relies on it; it is not a new change. Military goods fall under national rules and Directive 2009/43/EC, not under this Regulation.

notice: Each entry gives the primary source and one sentence of it, copied word for word, and the day we last read it. It is a reading aid for suppliers, not legal advice. Where a point is not settled by a text we could read, the status says unconfirmed.
